title: SS27 Women's Trim Market Strategy
summary: Where to spend on trims in a low-growth, cost-pressured 2027: use trims to refresh core shapes, sell decorative trims as add-ons, and keep labour-heavy embellishment for premium pieces.

sections.heading: The market context
sections.body:
Fashion is expected to stay in low single-digit growth in 2027, and FashionUnited's outlook argues that the question is how much growth will cost<sup>[1]</sup>. Freight, energy and financing costs remain high, and excess stock ties up cash and forces markdowns<sup>[1]</sup>. In the mid-market, promotional pressure and competition from luxury and value players squeeze margins<sup>[1]</sup>. Since 19 July 2026, large companies in the EU may not destroy certain unsold apparel, accessories and footwear<sup>[1]</sup>.

In that climate, trims are a low-risk way to update a range: they change how a core piece looks without new patterns, new fabrics or new production runs.

sections.heading: Build, test, sell through, exit
sections.body:
| Action | Trims | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Build | Belts, ribbon ties and bows, lace edging | Rising on the runway<sup>[2]</sup><sup>[3]</sup>; low cost; work across price points |
| Test | Fringe, visible fastenings (Velcro, cross-lacing, sequinned snaps), brooches | Early signals<sup>[2]</sup><sup>[3]</sup><sup>[4]</sup>; higher fashion risk |
| Sell through | Lingerie lace, crochet trims | At their height; avoid new depth |
| Premium only | 3D petals, crystal and bead embroidery | Hand labour; cost justified only at higher prices |

sections.heading: By market
sections.body:
- **Europe:** with the unsold-goods destruction ban<sup>[1]</sup>, keep trims modular and removable so unsold stock can be reworked.
- **India and the Gulf:** embroidery, lace and ribbon suit festive and modest dressing; India's economy grew 7.8% year on year in the second quarter of 2026<sup>[1]</sup>.
- **United States:** belts and add-on accessories support units per transaction where spending growth is modest<sup>[1]</sup>.
- **Hot-climate markets:** light trims (ribbon, rolled hems) suit single-layer summer clothes.

design_implications:
- Design core pieces with trim positions in mind (belt loops, ribbon channels, removable corsage pins).
- Standardise trim suppliers across themes to raise order quantities and cut cost.
commercial_implications:
- Budget trims as a share of the cost price per tier, with hand-applied decoration kept to premium.
- Track sell-through by trim variant and reorder the winners in season.
- Price separately sold trims (belts, corsages, brooches) to lift the average basket.
